Colota is an open-source GPS tracking app that sends your location to your own server over HTTP(S). It works offline, supports geofencing, and doesn't share any data except with your configured backends.

 Tracking Profiles - Automatically adjust GPS interval, distance filter and sync settings based on conditions like charging, Android Auto, Wi-Fi, a Bluetooth device, speed or stationary detection

izzyondroid:com.gitlab.giwiniswut.rwremo.name: SDRemount
izzyondroid:com.gitlab.giwiniswut.rwremo.summary: remounts the SD Card to allow write access
izzyondroid:com.gitlab.giwiniswut.rwremo.description:
Remember how google decided in 2013 that android needs a new and fancy framework for storage access?
 Frustrated of how they took away external storage write access because of this, as if to test drive the change on android devices with an SD Card (i.e. not Google devices) before enforcing it with internal storages as well for apps targeting and running on android 10 and above?
 Just want back write access to your sd card?
 Well now there's an app for that!
 Requirements: 
 A device with an SD Card slot
 Root access, since the app remounts some stuff
 Android 8.0 or later (but if you are running android 6.0.1, 7.0 or 7.1, it shouldn't hurt to just give it a shot)
 The approach currently used by this app definitely only applies to devices running android 6 or later. It has successfully been tested with devices running android 8.1, 9 and 10 and unsucsessfully on devices running android 7.1, 6.0.1 and 5.1.
 For further information consult the wiki .
 How to use it: 
 Install
 Launch once
 Grant permanent root access
 Insert or remount some storage
 Profit!
 Notes: 
 The app must be launched at least once or else the system won't ever run it. This is a security mechanism of the Android platform to protect users from apps they've never launched and maybe never wanted to use or install.
 This restriction can be removed by installing the app as a privileged app, i.e. by writing the apk file to /system/priv-app .
 Upon the first mount with this app installed, i.e. when you actively need to grant root access, it is possible that the app will do nothing. This is because the app will currently be terminated if it has to wait more than a few seconds for root access. Once root access has already been granted and the app is immediately given root access every time it needs it, everything should work as expected.

Amarok is an Android application which enables you to hide your private files & apps with just one click.
 Often, we resort to complex encryptors to secure our files and apps, aiming to shield them from prying eyes. These encryptors, while effective, tend to be slow and resource-intensive, making the encryption of large files such as videos and music a daunting task. Despite their robust security, these methods are often overkill for the average user who simply wish to keep their private files and apps out of unintentional reach.

 Features 
 User-Friendly : Easily hide files and applications with a single click.
 Rapid and Efficient Large File Hiding : Hides by altering only file name and signature, unaffected by file size.
 Root-Free Application Hiding : Makes apps vanish from the launcher. Compatible with Root, Shizuku, Dhizuku, and DSM modes.
 Panic button : Use a floating button to quickly hide applications and files in urgent scenarios.
 Quick Settings Tile : A control center toggle for immediate hiding, bypassing the need to launch the app.
 App Lock : Secure Amarok access with a password or fingerprint.
 Pleasant Interface : Clean Material3 design.
 Please be aware that Amarok is not an encryption software , but rather a tool for hiding things. We strongly advise against using Amarok to protect confidential files and applications.

fdroid:bombvault.halleluja.design.name: BombVault
fdroid:bombvault.halleluja.design.summary: Watch and open the BombVault backup servers you run yourself.
fdroid:bombvault.halleluja.design.description:
BombVault is a backup tool you run yourself, on Unraid or anywhere Docker runs. It backs up containers, virtual machines, the flash drive and folders with restic. This app is its companion on your phone: it shows what your servers are doing and opens each one's dashboard. The backups themselves run on your servers, never on the phone.
What you can do
• See every server in your group on one screen, with the newest lines of its activity log
• Open the whole activity log and switch between servers
• Open a server's dashboard in the app, without typing its password once the phone is paired
• Pick the language, light or dark, an accent colour and the corners, or let the app take its look from your first server
To pair, scan the QR code your BombVault shows under Settings → Pairing, or type its twelve words. Every server in the group appears at once. You can also add a single server by its address.
The activity log reaches the app through a relay: by default the project's relay at parleyport.halleluja.design, or your own ParleyPort if you enter its address on your servers. Requests and answers are end-to-end encrypted with a key that comes from your words, so the relay passes them on without being able to read them. When a server does not answer at its own address, away from home for example, the app opens its dashboard through the relay as well. The app shows no ads, tracks nothing and needs no account.
You need a running BombVault server. BombVault is free and open source under the AGPL-3.0: https://github.com/junkerderprovinz/bombvault
The app is new and changes quickly, and an update to your server can need an update to the app as well. Please report problems on GitHub.
The app uses the camera only to scan the QR code.

fdroid:dev.glyfen.app.summary: Offline OCR for Android. Search your photos by text, entirely on-device.
fdroid:dev.glyfen.app.description:
Glyfen is an offline-first OCR app for Android that lets you search your photo library by text content. All processing happens entirely on your device — no cloud uploads, no internet required.
Point Glyfen at your photo folders and it scans every image for text using PaddleOCR. Receipts, documents, screenshots, business cards, labels — if an image contains printed text, Glyfen extracts it and makes it searchable.
A note on speed: because all OCR runs on your device, scanning takes time — and you always start it yourself. Glyfen never scans automatically or on a schedule. How long a scan takes depends on how many images it covers and your phone's hardware, so a large library on an older phone can take a while. Once you start a scan it keeps running even while you use other apps, and it resumes automatically if it's interrupted. Added new photos? Just run a scan again to index them.
Once scanned, your photos become searchable. Type a word and Glyfen lists every image whose text contains it, with a preview of the recognized text. Full-text search is powered by SQLite FTS5 for fast results even across thousands of indexed images.
Key features:
- Offline OCR: All text recognition runs on-device using PaddleOCR. No network connection, ever.
- Full-text search: Find any receipt, note, or screenshot by the words inside it, in seconds, powered by SQLite FTS5.
- Latin-script first: Recognition and dictionary correction are tuned for English and Latin scripts. The underlying PP-OCRv5 model also recognizes Chinese, Japanese, Korean, Cyrillic, Arabic, and more.
- Batch scanning: You pick the folders and start the scan yourself; Glyfen then processes them on-device and keeps running while you use other apps. Speed scales with how many images you scan and your phone's hardware.
- Private by design: No analytics SDKs, no ads, no accounts, no tracking. Nothing is ever sent automatically. Optional diagnostics and telemetry are off by default and only leave your device if you choose to share a bug report.
- EXIF-aware: Correctly handles rotated camera photos.
- Format support: JPEG, PNG, WebP, and HEIF/HEIC (Android 9+).
- Local-only storage: OCR results stay in a private database on your device and are never uploaded.
- Crash recovery: Scans resume from where they left off after interruption.
- Open source: Built from source and fully auditable, published on F-Droid.
Glyfen is free software, built from source and published on F-Droid. No ads, no accounts, no tracking.
Permissions: None requested up-front. You pick which folders Glyfen can read using the system folder picker — Glyfen never sees anything outside the folders you grant. No camera, microphone, or location access requested.

Vinegar shows who owns the brands you're shopping for, directly on product pages.
 How it works 
- On supported retailer product pages, Vinegar reads the product brand from the page and looks it up against Vinegar's ownership database.
- An on-page card shows the parent company, subsidiaries, and related ownership info.
- You can switch between a panel or floating display, or hide the card from the popup.
 Supported retailers 
- Amazon (multiple regional sites)
- Walmart and Target requires an active premium subscription
 Features 
- Personal avoid list synced with your Vinegar account
 Account & privacy 
- Sign-in opens getvinegar.com in a new tab; the extension stores a token locally for API requests.
- Only the brand name is sent for lookups, not full page URLs, prices, cart contents, or purchase history.
- No third-party analytics or tracking. Requests go to getvinegar.com only.
 Links opened from the extension (only when you click them): sign-in, contribute a correction, report a claim, or open support tickets.

apple-macos:6826967725.name: Just Call: Private Video Chat
apple-macos:6826967725.description:
Just Call is the fastest way to get someone on a video call. Tap Video Invite, share the link, and you're talking. No account, no phone number, no sign-up.
PRIVATE BY DESIGN
• Peer-to-peer: audio and video travel directly between devices whenever your network allows. On restrictive networks, an encrypted relay keeps the call connected.
• No account required. Just a name and an optional photo, shared only with the people you call.
• Chat history stays on your phone and is deleted after 24 hours.
MADE FOR REAL CONVERSATIONS
• Video and voice calls
• Incoming calls ring like a regular iPhone call, even when your phone is locked
• Call back people you've talked to from your recent contacts
• Chat, stickers and photo sharing during a call
• Share a call link or a QR code. The other person can join from any web browser, no app needed
• Available in 10 languages
Just Call keeps the path to a conversation short: minimal setup, minimal stored data, and nothing between you and the person you want to talk to.

apple-macos:6755543962.name: FrostNote: Aisle Shopping List
apple-macos:6755543962.description:
Stop doubling back. FrostNote organizes any shopping list by aisle — groceries, hardware, home goods, you name it — so you move through the store once and leave.
YOUR STORE, YOUR AISLE ORDER
Set up your store's aisle layout, then assign each item its aisle as you build your list. FrostNote groups and sorts everything in the order you'll actually walk the store. Running the same list every week? Reset it with one tap — your items and their aisle assignments stay right where you left them.
ALWAYS HAVE A BACKUP PLAN
Add an alternate to any item. If Fuji Apples are out, you've already thought ahead with Gala Apples as your backup.
SHOP AT TWO STORES
Configure a backup store alongside your primary one. Assign items to aisles in both, and your list stays sensibly sorted whether you end up at your usual spot or somewhere else.
SHARE WITH YOUR WHOLE HOUSEHOLD
Everyone in the house can add, check off, and see updates in real time. No more texts asking "did you grab the milk?" Household sharing keeps everyone on the same list.
WORKS EVEN WITHOUT WIFI
FrostNote is offline-first. You can view and update your list with no connection — changes sync automatically when you're back online.
FLEXIBLE PLANS FOR EVERY HOUSEHOLD
• Free — full app features, supported by ads
• Ad-Free — one-time purchase, removes ads, syncs across all your devices
• Premium — everything in Ad-Free, plus real-time sharing with up to 5 household members
Your data is always yours. Upgrade or cancel any time — your lists never disappear.
SIGN IN YOUR WAY
Sign in with Apple, Sign in with Google, Passkeys, or a classic email account. Or skip sign-in entirely and try the app locally with no account needed.
Available on iPhone, iPad, and Mac.

apple-macos:6821051211.name: Territory Tactics: Map War
apple-macos:6821051211.description:
Territory Tactics is a strategy game of conquest on real maps, and nobody waits for a turn. Each round, all players place their new troops together, then give their orders in secret, at the same time. Then the whole table watches every order play out on one board.
HOW A ROUND GOES
New troops arrive and you place them on your own land.
You give up to three orders: attack a neighbour, move an army through land you hold, or dig in to defend.
Each attack shows its chance to win before you commit. One roll decides the battle.
When everyone is ready, the orders are played one at a time, starting with the weakest player.
WHAT YOU PLAN AROUND
Terrain. Mountains defend better, forests cost the attacker more troops, and lowlands pay extra troops.
Regions. Hold a whole region and it pays a bonus, such as more troops, an extra order or stronger attacks.
Landmarks. Each one pays a troop every round and defends better. In two of the three ways to play, they decide the winner.
Augments. On set rounds everyone picks one of three powers and keeps it for the match. There are 52 of them in three tiers, and the player in last place is offered a fourth choice.
Crates and world events. Supply crates, uprisings, plagues and earthquakes are announced a round ahead, so you can plan for them.
THREE WAYS A MATCH CAN END
Total conquest: be the last side on the map.
Capture the cities: hold 5 landmarks for one full round.
12 rounds: capture the cities, or hold the most landmarks when round 12 ends.
THE MAPS
The Grand World: the whole world in 348 territories on six continents, for up to ten players. Hold a whole continent and it pays.
Europe, in 95 territories from Iceland to Persia, reaching into North Africa, the Middle East and the Caucasus.
Riga, in 81 territories drawn from real map data, with the Daugava, its islands and its bridges.
Istanbul, in 85 territories drawn from its real neighbourhoods, on both shores of the Bosphorus.
And the World, in 170 territories, in beta.
ALONE OR WITH FRIENDS
Play alone against bots. It needs no connection, and you can switch the clock off and think for as long as you like.
Or open a room and send its link or its five-letter code. Up to ten people can sit at the table on the world maps, and six on the others, and bots can fill the empty seats. Nobody needs an account to play: you type a name and sit down.
TEAMS AND SIGNALS
Every side for itself, or teams of any size: two against two, three against one, or anything else. During a round you can send the table fixed signals, offer a truce, or react to a battle. There is no free chat.
GREAT BATTLES
When two armies of 50 or more meet, the board cuts to the battle itself for a few seconds: the two armies face each other on that land's own ground, fire their volleys and fall as the battle decides. Skip it with a tap, or switch it off.
THE TABLE
